dogecoin.text: With that kilowatt requirement, it would take 12,480 kilowatt hours to mine enough $doge to equal one $BTC, which only requires 707 kilowatt hours.  Very logical.

(1/2) Ah yes.  $TSLA might accept $DOGE as payment but not $BTC.  It takes 707 kilowatt hours to mine one bitcoin, but takes 0.12 kilowatt hours to mine one doge.  At the $doge price of $0.50 each, it would take 104,000 doge to equal the $BTC price of $52,000.
